scope: Ten primary-source business-system/workflow/document/AI repository candidates for Ariadne. Broad bounded review, not an exhaustive scan of all GitHub, a security audit or installation qualification.
method: Read existing Ariadne capability documentation to distinguish installed features from genuinely missing integrations.
Used GitHub connector repository/file reads for canonical sources and license/README blob identities.
Read live unauthenticated official GitHub REST repository and releases/latest JSON; metadata contains no account credentials.
Read official deployment/offline documentation. Default branches are moving references; observed file blob IDs and release tags identify evidence.
limits: No repository code, installer, workflow or skill was run; no models/dependencies installed.
No owner configurations, services, microphone, OS tasks or network policy were changed; E: was not accessed.
Activity and publisher security fixes are evidence of maintenance, not proof of safety.
Future deployment needs exact dependency/image/model closure, permissions, license review and disconnected qualification.
existing_baseline: Ariadne already provides local business records, fixed office output/analytics/optimization workers, OCR/knowledge, reviewed connectors/MCP, fixed Node-RED routes, checked routines and ERPNext preparation. A prepared template is not a running external business service.
recommendation: Keep Ariadne's engine and current deterministic tools. Qualify a read-first adapter to ONE business records system, compare ERPNext with Dolibarr, add dedicated CRM/document lifecycle only when the selected ERP lacks the needed workflow. Use selected integration pieces rather than another default agent/workflow platform.

candidates.name: ERPNext
candidates.best_use: One operational system for sales, purchasing, inventory, manufacturing and accounting.
candidates.license: GPL-3.0; upstream and dependency notices retained
candidates.license_notes: Observed upstream license.txt header. Framework and each added app keep their own terms.
candidates.offline: Local operations after complete provisioning; payment gateways, remote email and fresh exchange rates still require their services.
candidates.runtime: Linux/WSL/VM or container stack with Frappe, database and workers; not a native Windows plug-in.
candidates.existing_overlap: Ariadne already has balanced local business records, fixed reports and an ERPNext preparation route. Preparation is not a running ERP installation.
candidates.advancement: The observed release adds a BOM design workspace for STEP/CSV imports and design revision comparison: a useful bridge from Ariadne's CAD artifacts into manufacturing planning.
candidates.adapter: Start with read-only customers/items/stock and dated document IDs; then approval-bound draft quotations and purchase requests. Posting, payment, deletion and delivery need separate explicit authority.
candidates.cost: Engineering estimate: appreciable always-on database/queue/worker maintenance; no LLM required for routine ERP reads. Choose one ERP, not three.
candidates.requirements: Owner company chart of accounts, test company and scoped API credentials; separate database/files/encryption-key backup and restore plan.
risks: Ariadne's SQLite-only backup does not back up an external ERP database.
Versioned schema migrations and apps need pinned compatible versions.
Do not treat generated bookkeeping or tax reports as independently certified.
candidates.cost_basis: Qualitative engineering estimate; no runtime/resource/energy benchmark conducted.

candidates.name: Dolibarr
candidates.best_use: Small-business CRM, quotes, invoices, orders, stock and manufacturing modules.
candidates.license_notes: README explicitly permits GPL version 3 or later; COPYING observed.
candidates.offline: LAN/local records after PHP/server/database provisioning; external bank, mail and payment connectors remain connected functions.
candidates.runtime: PHP web server and MariaDB/MySQL/PostgreSQL; official README offers DoliWamp for Windows and Docker alternatives.
candidates.existing_overlap: Overlaps the proposed ERPNext system and Ariadne's lightweight business records.
candidates.advancement: Windows packaging is a practical alternative when the owner values a conventional business application over a larger Frappe stack; actual resource advantage remains unmeasured.
candidates.adapter: Read-only stock, counterparties and outstanding-document summaries first; validate API permissions before separately approved draft invoice creation.
candidates.cost: Engineering estimate: additional web/database maintenance. Benchmark against ERPNext using the same invoicing/stock tasks before selecting.
candidates.requirements: Test company, module choices, owner-created credentials and a coordinated database/documents backup.
risks: Do not install both ERP alternatives without a concrete need.
Plug-in/module licenses and security state differ from core.
A recent push is not a security assessment.
candidates.cost_basis: Qualitative engineering estimate; no runtime/resource/energy benchmark conducted.

candidates.name: Odoo Community
candidates.license: Community core LGPL-3.0; Enterprise and add-ons have separate terms
candidates.license_notes: Actual LICENSE file inspected; GitHub's detected NOASSERTION is not a substitute for the file. Community repository is not a grant to Enterprise features.
candidates.offline: Self-hosted core records can be local; external services, hosted AI and payment/email functionality are not disconnected capabilities.
candidates.runtime: Observed release.py requires Python 3.12-3.14 and PostgreSQL >=16. Source exposes a Windows service name; exact Windows deployment not qualified here.
candidates.existing_overlap: Substantial ERPNext/Dolibarr overlap; do not add as a third always-on business platform.
candidates.advancement: Broad module ecosystem and new 20.0 source series; select for a specific required module rather than marketing breadth.
candidates.adapter: A version-pinned service API wrapper with test records and owner-selected fields; no direct model SQL, application installation or generic administrator access.
candidates.cost: Engineering estimate: database, module upgrades and migrations add operational work; some desired features or add-ons can require commercial licensing.
candidates.requirements: Chosen Community modules, scoped service user and separate PostgreSQL/filestore recovery plan.
risks: GitHub releases/latest returned 404: source 20.0 is observed, but no precise release timestamp was established.
Not every capability listed by Odoo marketing belongs to Community.
Source/dependency support on this specific Windows box remains untested.
candidates.cost_basis: Qualitative engineering estimate; no runtime/resource/energy benchmark conducted.

candidates.name: Twenty
candidates.best_use: Structured CRM objects, opportunity pipelines and reviewable CRM app extensions.
candidates.license: Mostly AGPL-3.0 with Twenty Application Exception; selected SDK/UI/app packages MIT; Enterprise-marked code commercial
candidates.license_notes: LICENSE qualifications and the additional application-interface permission were read; this is not a claim every repository file is AGPL or MIT.
candidates.offline: Local CRM objects and views after provisioning; provider account authorization, email/calendar sync and cloud AI need external services.
candidates.runtime: Docker Compose server/worker, PostgreSQL and Redis. Upstream documents at least 2 GB RAM; that is a publisher minimum, not measured full-stack consumption.
candidates.existing_overlap: Adds durable deal/company/contact pipelines beyond Ariadne's simpler contacts; may duplicate the selected ERP's CRM.
candidates.advancement: Current README presents objects, views, workflows and agents as versioned application code, plus official app skills. The release includes changed application-account authorization and security dependency updates.
candidates.adapter: Read selected company/deal objects through fixed REST/GraphQL endpoints; stage draft field changes with exact record IDs and revisions; require approval for outreach and destructive mutations.
candidates.cost: Engineering estimate: extra persistent services and backups. No required model for CRUD; optional agent/provider usage has separate inference/API costs.
candidates.requirements: Scoped API credentials, selected objects and preserved encryption key as well as database backup.
risks: Official agent skills are research inputs, not automatically trusted authority or installed code.
Read current Enterprise/application-exception terms before bundling.
Email/calendar accounts require owner setup and connectivity.
candidates.cost_basis: Qualitative engineering estimate; no runtime/resource/energy benchmark conducted.

candidates.name: Paperless-ngx
candidates.best_use: Managed invoice/receipt/contract inbox, OCR archive, tags and document lifecycle.
candidates.license_notes: Observed upstream GPLv3 LICENSE; software license does not grant rights to uploaded documents.
candidates.offline: Preloaded local ingestion/OCR/search can operate disconnected; mail ingestion and external enrichment cannot refresh without their sources.
candidates.runtime: Docker Compose recommended; PostgreSQL recommended for new installations, queue and OCR dependencies. Optional Tika/Office support adds services.
candidates.existing_overlap: Ariadne already extracts/OCRs/searches documents. New value is business document ownership, metadata, consumption queue and lifecycle, not another OCR engine alone.
candidates.advancement: 3.3.4 is a security maintenance release updating affected trust/dependency components; choose a patched pinned image rather than a convenient older tutorial.
candidates.adapter: Read-only document ID/metadata and explicitly selected text snapshots into Ariadne with content hashes; reviewed tagging before any deletion or original-file replacement.
candidates.cost: Engineering estimate: CPU OCR and document storage plus persistent queue/database. No LLM required; reuse current extraction where it meets the need.
candidates.requirements: Owner-selected consume folder, access scopes, retention rules and coordinated database/media/classifier/config backups.
risks: Ingested invoices may contain malicious instructions and sensitive records.
Do not treat OCR totals as verified accounting entries.
Exact offline and Windows-container behavior must be qualified after provisioning.
candidates.cost_basis: Qualitative engineering estimate; no runtime/resource/energy benchmark conducted.

candidates.name: Activepieces
candidates.best_use: Reusable business integration pieces exposed as narrowly selected workflow/MCP operations.
candidates.license: MIT community code outside explicit Enterprise paths; Enterprise code commercial; third-party component terms separate
candidates.license_notes: Actual rootLICENSE overrides an oversimplified MIT badge. Recommended upstream installer can choose Enterprise edition; free versus licensed feature set must be frozen.
candidates.offline: Local pieces and preloaded runtime can operate locally; SaaS pieces still require provider credentials and connectivity. Network-gapped claims require checking the selected edition and piece closure.
candidates.runtime: Current official guide: Docker Compose 2, PostgreSQL, Redis, app/worker; Windows via WSL2; publisher minimum 2 vCPU / 4 GB RAM, not a measured Ariadne budget.
candidates.existing_overlap: Ariadne already has fixed Node-RED routes, connectors, schedules and checked routines. Reuse specific pieces only when they add a missing integration.
candidates.advancement: Pieces can be exposed as MCP tools. Latest observed hotfix fixes an unauthenticated webhook-triggered API-process crash, making exact patch selection material.
candidates.adapter: Freeze a small tool/schema allowlist; keep provider secrets out of prompts; reuse Ariadne approvals and no-replay receipts instead of inheriting auto-retries blindly.
candidates.cost: Engineering estimate: four service roles, database/queue storage and upgrade work. Prefer existing Node-RED/fixed adapters unless a needed piece earns the overhead.
candidates.requirements: Reviewed Community-only build or clearly selected edition, encryption keys, scoped provider credentials and database-volume backups.
risks: Do not pipe the upstream install script into a shell as part of this research.
Upstream defaults can launch multiple workers and collide with Ariadne port8080.
Backing up only the install folder omits PostgreSQL Docker-volume state.
candidates.cost_basis: Qualitative engineering estimate; no runtime/resource/energy benchmark conducted.

candidates.name: Invoice Ninja
candidates.best_use: Quotes, invoicing, time/expense/project records and client billing portal.
candidates.license: Elastic License2.0, source-available; not a permissive/OSI-open-source default
candidates.license_notes: ELv2 restricts providing substantial functionality as a hosted/managed service and removing protected notices/license mechanisms. Additional commercial embedding/branding questions need explicit terms.
candidates.offline: Local draft billing records/PDFs after provisioning; actual payment processing, delivery and remote client access require their networks/services.
candidates.runtime: Laravel/PHP self-hosted server/VM or Docker and database; Windows desktop client is not the complete server stack.
candidates.existing_overlap: Invoicing may already belong to the chosen ERP; this is a narrower alternative, not a reason for two ledgers.
candidates.advancement: Current release has scheduler/API fixes; mature API could support draft quote/invoice production.
candidates.adapter: Owner-managed optional endpoint for read-only invoices and approval-bound draft quotes. Sending, charging cards, refunds and invoice finalization remain distinct actions.
candidates.cost: Engineering estimate: PHP/database/queue administration; optional branding/commercial terms and payment-provider fees are separate from model cost.
candidates.requirements: Owner company/tax settings, scoped API token, test customer and preserved application encryption secret.
risks: Do not label the whole app MIT/open-source because a client component has different terms.
No hosted resale/wrapping assumption for an appliance used by anyone.
Exact offline PDF renderer closure still needs qualification.
candidates.cost_basis: Qualitative engineering estimate; no runtime/resource/energy benchmark conducted.

candidates.name: n8n
candidates.best_use: Owner-operated business workflow canvas and many service integrations.
candidates.license: Sustainable Use License; Enterprise-marked files separately licensed
candidates.license_notes: Current license permits own internal business or non-commercial/personal use; distribution/provision to others is restricted to free non-commercial purposes under those terms. Not a blanket permissive appliance redistribution license.
candidates.offline: Locally provisioned engine and local nodes can run disconnected; provider APIs, live SaaS triggers and external AI are connected dependencies.
candidates.runtime: Docker or self-hosted Node deployment, persistent data and optional scaled workers/database; exact selected architecture must be pinned.
candidates.existing_overlap: Duplicates Ariadne routines/schedules plus existing Node-RED and connector administration.
candidates.advancement: Latest observed patch is today; extensive AI/workflow integrations are useful discovery material, but breadth does not overcome license or maintenance constraints.
candidates.adapter: If owner selects it separately, expose specific reviewed read operations and bounded commands through fixed endpoints; keep Ariadne approval as the authority boundary.
candidates.cost: Engineering estimate: another service, secret store and workflow execution history; optional Enterprise/API costs. No measured advantage over existing routines established.
candidates.requirements: Chosen licensing arrangement, provider credentials, encryption-key backup and reviewed node supply chain.
risks: Many integrations and AI nodes need Internet/API accounts.
Automatic retries can duplicate consequential external actions.
Community node code is not implicitly trusted by repository popularity.
candidates.cost_basis: Qualitative engineering estimate; no runtime/resource/energy benchmark conducted.

candidates.name: Windmill
candidates.best_use: Versioned internal scripts, forms, API jobs and reviewed code workflows.
candidates.license: Non-Enterprise source generally AGPLv3; clients/OpenAPI Apache-2.0; proprietary Enterprise portions; prebuilt Community images/binaries have additional restrictions
candidates.license_notes: Actual LICENSE states prebuilt Community includes non-public/proprietary material and restricts selling, wrapping, managed service and commercial embedding absent agreement. A non-Enterprise source build is a different licensing route.
candidates.offline: Cached code, language runtimes, packages and local targets can be local; Git sync, remote packages, SaaS and hosted AI remain external.
candidates.runtime: Server, workers and persistent database; explicit language/package cache and isolated worker boundaries required.
candidates.existing_overlap: A second workflow scheduler/code execution authority alongside Ariadne and existing fixed workers.
candidates.advancement: Current docs describe AI building in workspace forks with review/promotion and separated workers; latest patch includes MCP runnable fixes.
candidates.adapter: Take the review-before-promotion pattern; evaluate only a preapproved typed internal job endpoint. Never grant an LLM a generic Bash/PowerShell resource by default.
candidates.cost: Engineering estimate: service/database/worker and multi-language cache maintenance; hosted/commercial features add separate recurring obligations.
candidates.requirements: Explicit source/build or product license choice, separate worker identities, scoped resource secrets and backups.
risks: Do not redistribute or rebrand a downloaded Community image as unrestricted AGPL software.
Script sandboxing still depends on worker deployment configuration.
Adding it merely for agents duplicates existing lifecycle/approval surfaces.
candidates.cost_basis: Qualitative engineering estimate; no runtime/resource/energy benchmark conducted.

candidates.name: LightRAG
candidates.best_use: Relationship-aware answers over a sufficiently complex business document corpus.
candidates.license: MIT code; selected models/dependencies/data have separate terms
candidates.license_notes: Model/code licenses differ; official offline extras are not a grant for model weights or imported business records.
candidates.offline: Possible with local LLM/embedding/storage and complete package/tokenizer caches. Defaults or dynamically installed providers must be replaced/prefetched deliberately.
candidates.runtime: Python/API service or Docker; official offline group excludes heavy transformers/Torch/CUDA dependencies and recommends separating expensive parsing services.
candidates.existing_overlap: Ariadne already has lexical/hybrid knowledge, provenance and rich parsing. Add graph extraction only if a measured relationship-query failure justifies it.
candidates.advancement: Upstream has role-specific LLM configuration, contexts/citation support and an end-user workspace; useful isolation/evaluation ideas for business knowledge.
candidates.adapter: Run a separate benchmark over a copied non-sensitive corpus; compare answer evidence and total ingestion/query model calls against the existing index before any integration.
candidates.cost: Engineering estimate: graph extraction and regeneration add LLM work, storage and re-index cost; local inference still uses electricity/compute. Savings not established.
candidates.requirements: Pinned local model/tokenizer assets, citation-preserving corpus permissions and cache closure.
risks: Dynamic pip installation or tokenizer downloads can break an otherwise local deployment.
Wrong/omitted relationships can produce confident business answers.
Default cloud providers and unauthenticated compatible routes must not be inherited silently.
candidates.cost_basis: Qualitative engineering estimate; no runtime/resource/energy benchmark conducted.
